docs.title: ZEN API
docs.text:
Microscope services, protocol definitions, and reusable workflow utilities.

Package Documented version zen_api 2026.05.1 zen_api_utils 0.1.0

Getting started | Utilities guide | Documented versions

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
The generated API and utility helpers are separate Python distributions. Both support Python 3.12-3.15 (>=3.12,<3.16). Obtain the matching authorized wheels and install them in the same environment:

python -m pip install zen_api-2026.05.1-py3-none-any.whl
python -m pip install zen_api_utils-0.1.0-py3-none-any.whl
python -m pip check

ZEN must be running with its API enabled to execute microscope commands. See the utilities guide for available helpers and optional OME-Zarr support.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text:
All notable changes to the ZEN API project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on Keep a Changelog. Package versions follow the format YYYY.MM.PATCH.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Maintained zen_api_utils package for reusable acquisition, hardware, streaming, and OME-Zarr utilities
  • MkDocs API reference documentation generated from the Python package using mkdocstrings (Material theme)
  • New generate_mkdocs_pages.py script to auto-generate API reference pages from the zen_api module tree
  • New $BUILD_MKDOCS option in create_python_packages.ps1
  • GitHub Actions workflow for building package artifacts and deploying versioned MkDocs documentation to GitHub Pages
  • Versioned documentation support via mike

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Both zen_api and zen_api_utils now declare Python 3.12-3.15 only (>=3.12,<3.16); Python 3.10 and 3.11 support is dropped.
  • Package and documentation publication is gated on compatibility tests for Python 3.12, 3.13, 3.14, and 3.15.
  • Moved reusable streaming and OME-Zarr functionality into zen_api_utils, including the zenapi-stream2omezarr command
  • Replaced WeasyPrint with Playwright (Chromium) for HTML-to-PDF conversion — no native GTK/Pango libraries required
  • generate_python_wrappers.py can now resolve protoc from PATH when no explicit install path is provided
  • Local PowerShell packaging uses the zenapi conda environment by default

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Streaming example now selects the working PySide6 backend before importing pyqtgraph and qasync
  • generate_python_wrappers.py and build_wheel_package.py now propagate exit codes via sys.exit() so failures are correctly detected by the build script
  • Added $LASTEXITCODE checks after git checkout and git pull in create_python_packages.ps1 to fail fast on git errors
  • Quoted --label, --proto-root, and --output-dir arguments in docbuilder invocation to handle paths/labels with spaces
  • Fixed typo in $ZEN_API_DOCS_LABEL separator (Version:- → Version:)

docs.title: Added in 2026.05.1
docs.text:
• Proto definitions for ZEN Release 3.14 (Spring 2026)
  • PDF conversion support via WeasyPrint in clean_html_badges.py
  • Automatic fontconfig setup for WeasyPrint on Windows
  • --delete_cleaned_html flag to remove temporary cleaned HTML files after processing
  • HTML-to-Markdown conversion with GitHub-flavored Markdown support
  • Copyright header injection into generated Python files (build_wheel_package.py)
  • Invoke-CondaPython helper to avoid conda run file-locking issues on Windows
  • Comprehensive build instructions in Instructions.md

docs.title: Added in 2025.10.1
docs.text:
• Initial public release of ZEN API proto definitions (ZEN Release 3.13, Autumn 2025)
  • Python wrapper generation from .proto files using betterproto
  • Wheel package build pipeline (create_python_packages.ps1)
  • HTML documentation generation via zenapi-docbuilder
  • HTML badge cleaning script (clean_html_badges.py)
  • Azure DevOps CI/CD compatible logging

docs.title: Documented Versions
docs.text:
Package Documented version zen_api 2026.05.1 zen_api_utils 0.1.0

This site is a snapshot of these two source versions. They are independently versioned packages; the site version follows zen_api. Utility-only releases do not change archived documentation automatically. CI tests utilities against the matching API wheel before publishing this combined site.

docs.title: ZEN API
docs.text: Python wrappers for the ZEN API, enabling programmatic control of ZEISS microscopy software via gRPC.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
This package is not available on PyPI. Install from the wheel file:

pip install zen_api-<version>-py3-none-any.whl

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python 3.12-3.15 (>=3.12,<3.16)
  • betterproto == 2.0.0b7

docs.title: API Domains
docs.text:
The ZEN API is organized into several domains:

Domain Description acquisition Experiment and image acquisition services application Application-level composition services common Shared data types and enumerations em Electron microscopy hardware and workflow services hardware Microscope hardware control (stages, axes) lm Light microscopy acquisition, hardware, live scan, and slide scan services workflows Automated workflow and job management services

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
from zen_api.acquisition.v1beta import ExperimentServiceStub

# Connect to ZEN API server
# (requires ZEN software running with API server enabled)

docs.title: ZEN API Utilities
docs.text: Reusable, headless helpers for applications built on the generated zen_api protobuf and gRPC package.

docs.title: Contents
docs.text: The API reference includes connection and logging helpers, experiment and acquisition-plan parsing, hardware helpers, stage and sample-carrier models, workflow helpers, TCP/IP control helpers, and streaming utilities.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Install a matching local zen_api wheel first, then install this package:

pip install zen_api-<version>-py3-none-any.whl
pip install zen_api_utils-<version>-py3-none-any.whl

OME-Zarr support is optional:

pip install "zen_api_utils[omezarr]"

docs.title: Clone
docs.text:
Clones an already loaded experiment. Useful when one wants to clone an experiment before modifying it in order to preserve the original experiment. This method returns the info needed to reference the cloned experiment.

rpc Clone (zen_api.acquisition.v1beta.ExperimentServiceCloneRequest) returns (zen_api.acquisition.v1beta.ExperimentServiceCloneResponse);

Request: zen_api.acquisition.v1beta.ExperimentServiceCloneRequest

Response: zen_api.acquisition.v1beta.ExperimentServiceCloneResponse

docs.title: Delete
docs.text:
Deletes an experiment file from the predefined location on disk. It does not delete the corresponding loaded experiment instance.

rpc Delete (zen_api.acquisition.v1beta.ExperimentServiceDeleteRequest) returns (zen_api.acquisition.v1beta.ExperimentServiceDeleteResponse);

docs.text:
Gets status of an experiment. The information is updated in interval (several times per seconds). As a result, some status updates could be skipped.

docs.text:

docs.title: RegisterOnStatusChanged
docs.text:
Register on experiment status changed events. The information is updated in interval (several times per seconds). As a result, some status updates could be skipped. The notifications can be retrieved for experiments which are active at the time the method is invoked. If the method is invoked after an experiment is finished, the call will throw an exception.

rpc RegisterOnStatusChanged (zen_api.acquisition.v1beta.ExperimentServiceRegisterOnStatusChangedRequest) returns (stream zen_api.acquisition.v1beta.ExperimentServiceRegisterOnStatusChangedResponse);

Request: zen_api.acquisition.v1beta.ExperimentServiceRegisterOnStatusChangedRequest

Response: zen_api.acquisition.v1beta.ExperimentServiceRegisterOnStatusChangedResponse

docs.title: RunExperiment
docs.text:
Executes an experiment and waits until the experiment execution is finished. This means that the method will block until the experiment was successfully completed, it fails, or it is cancelled. If the call is interrupted (e.g., caller is not available anymore) the experiment will be stopped.

rpc RunExperiment (zen_api.acquisition.v1beta.ExperimentServiceRunExperimentRequest) returns (zen_api.acquisition.v1beta.ExperimentServiceRunExperimentResponse);

Request: zen_api.acquisition.v1beta.ExperimentServiceRunExperimentRequest

Response: zen_api.acquisition.v1beta.ExperimentServiceRunExperimentResponse

docs.title: RunSnap
docs.text:
Acquires a single snap image with the activated channels in the specified experiment and waits until the process of acquiring snap is finished. This means that the method will block until the experiment was successfully completed, it fails, or it is cancelled. If the call is interrupted (e.g., caller is not available anymore) the snap will be stopped.

rpc RunSnap (zen_api.acquisition.v1beta.ExperimentServiceRunSnapRequest) returns (zen_api.acquisition.v1beta.ExperimentServiceRunSnapResponse);

Request: zen_api.acquisition.v1beta.ExperimentServiceRunSnapRequest

Response: zen_api.acquisition.v1beta.ExperimentServiceRunSnapResponse

docs.title: Save
docs.text:
Saves a loaded experiment to the predefined location on disk.

rpc Save (zen_api.acquisition.v1beta.ExperimentServiceSaveRequest) returns (zen_api.acquisition.v1beta.ExperimentServiceSaveResponse);

Request: zen_api.acquisition.v1beta.ExperimentServiceSaveRequest

Response: zen_api.acquisition.v1beta.ExperimentServiceSaveResponse

docs.title: StartContinuous
docs.text:
Starts the continuous with the activated channels in the specified experiment and waits for the acquisition to start. After that point continuous will run until it is explicitly stopped or it fails - even if the caller is not available anymore.

rpc StartContinuous (zen_api.acquisition.v1beta.ExperimentServiceStartContinuousRequest) returns (google.protobuf.Empty);

Request: zen_api.acquisition.v1beta.ExperimentServiceStartContinuousRequest

Response: google.protobuf.Empty

docs.title: StartExperiment
docs.text:
Starts the process of executing an experiment and waits for the acquisition to start. After that point the experiment will either run to completion (successful or not) or until it is explicitly stopped - even if the caller is not available anymore.

rpc StartExperiment (zen_api.acquisition.v1beta.ExperimentServiceStartExperimentRequest) returns (zen_api.acquisition.v1beta.ExperimentServiceStartExperimentResponse);

Request: zen_api.acquisition.v1beta.ExperimentServiceStartExperimentRequest

Response: zen_api.acquisition.v1beta.ExperimentServiceStartExperimentResponse

docs.title: StartLive
docs.text:
Starts live with the requested track in the specified experiment and waits for the acquisition to start. After that point live will run until it is explicitly stopped or it fails - even if the caller is not available anymore.

rpc StartLive (zen_api.acquisition.v1beta.ExperimentServiceStartLiveRequest) returns (google.protobuf.Empty);

Request: zen_api.acquisition.v1beta.ExperimentServiceStartLiveRequest

Response: google.protobuf.Empty

docs.title: StartSnap
docs.text:
Starts the process of acquiring a single snap image with the activated channels in the specified experiment and waits for the acquisition to start. After that point the snap will either run to completion (successful or not) or until it is explicitly stopped - even if the caller is not available anymore.

rpc StartSnap (zen_api.acquisition.v1beta.ExperimentServiceStartSnapRequest) returns (zen_api.acquisition.v1beta.ExperimentServiceStartSnapResponse);

Request: zen_api.acquisition.v1beta.ExperimentServiceStartSnapRequest

Response: zen_api.acquisition.v1beta.ExperimentServiceStartSnapResponse

docs.title: Stop
docs.text:
Stops the specified experiment or one of the active experiments if the experiment ID is not provided. This will stop any type of experiment (i.e., experiment, snap, continuous, live) if it is active and known to this service. This method returns the info needed to reference the stopped experiment.

rpc Stop (zen_api.acquisition.v1beta.ExperimentServiceStopRequest) returns (zen_api.acquisition.v1beta.ExperimentServiceStopResponse);

Request: zen_api.acquisition.v1beta.ExperimentServiceStopRequest

Response: zen_api.acquisition.v1beta.ExperimentServiceStopResponse

docs.title: Message FrameData
docs.text:
A simple container for the frame data. This can contain either a full frame or only a part of it (e.g., in case of partial acquisition when working with EM and LSM).

Field Number Type Presence Description experiment_id 1 string singular The ID of the experiment. frame_number 2 int32 singular The frame sequence number. One frame can represent either a single image taken by the camera or one full scan in case of partial acquisition. One frame can also contain multiple channels if they are acquired in the same image or scan. frame_position 3 zen_api.acquisition.v1beta.FramePosition singular The position of the full frame. frame_size 4 zen_api.common.v1.IntSize singular The size of the full frame (in pixels). frame_stage_position 5 zen_api.acquisition.v1beta.FrameStagePosition singular The stage position of the acquired full frame. scaling 6 zen_api.acquisition.v1beta.Scaling singular The scaling of the frame. pixel_data 7 zen_api.acquisition.v1beta.FramePixelData singular The pixel data of the frame. This can contain either the pixels of a full frame or only a part of it (e.g., a line or a rectangle in case of partial acquisition when working with EM and LSM).

docs.title: Message FramePixelData
docs.text:
A simple container for the frame pixel data. This can contain either the pixels of a full frame or only a part of it (e.g., a line or a rectangle in case of partial acquisition when working with EM and LSM).

Field Number Type Presence Description start_position 1 zen_api.common.v1.IntPoint singular The start position (in pixels) of the pixel data in the frame. Together with the size property, this represents the rectangle where the pixels are located inside the full frame. For ordinary acquisition this will be the top left corner of the frame, but for partial acquisition this can be any position inside the full frame relative to the top left corner. size 2 zen_api.common.v1.IntSize singular Size (in pixels) of the pixel data. Together with the start position property, this represents the rectangle where the pixels are located inside the full frame. For ordinary acquisition this will be the full frame size, but for partial acquisition this can be just one part of the full frame. pixel_type 3 zen_api.acquisition.v1beta.PixelType singular The pixel type of the frame. raw_data 4 bytes singular The raw pixel data. The value of individual pixels is contained in this container. The pixel values need to be extracted from the raw byte data. The number of bits needed to extract a single pixel from the raw byte data and the format it is stored in is determined by the pixel type property.

docs.title: Enum BeamState
docs.text:
Possible beam operating states.

Name Number Description BEAM_STATE_UNSPECIFIED 0 Default enum value. BEAM_STATE_UNKNOWN 1 Unknown indicates that this variable hasn't been assigned yet. This value should never occur. If you read this value, it's a bug. BEAM_STATE_ERROR 2 There is an error with the Gun or EHT and the beam cannot be used. BEAM_STATE_OFF 3 EHT is off. On FE-SEMs, the gun may be on, gun interfaces must be checked to discover gun state. On C-SEMs the EHT and gun are off, and there is no current on the filament. BEAM_STATE_TURNING_ON 4 The EHT (and gun for C-SEM) is turning on. BEAM_STATE_ON 5 Gun is on. Filament (if it exists) has full current. EHT is on. The beam can be used. BEAM_STATE_GOING_TO_STANDBY 6 The beam is going into the standby state. BEAM_STATE_STANDBY 7 Not all devices support this mode. This represents an intermediate state. The EVO and the FIB have standby states. BEAM_STATE_TURNING_OFF 8 The EHT is ramping down. On C-SEM, the gun and filament may also be shutting down.

docs.text:

Name Number Description CAMERA_ACQUISITION_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED 0 Default enum value. CAMERA_ACQUISITION_STATUS_UNKNOWN 1 Should not occur in an initialized system. CAMERA_ACQUISITION_STATUS_ERROR 2 The image acquisition device is in an error state and cannot be used. CAMERA_ACQUISITION_STATUS_IDLE 3 The image acquisition device is ready to perform a task. CAMERA_ACQUISITION_STATUS_BUSY 4 The image acquisition device is busy with other tasks and cannot be used for image acquisition. CAMERA_ACQUISITION_STATUS_LIVE_ACQUISITION 5 The system is performing a scan and will continue until explicitly asked to stop. We use the term "Live" instead of "Continuous" because in ZIS, "Continuous" means "a time series of snaps with no delay between and no scheduled end". CAMERA_ACQUISITION_STATUS_SINGLE_ACQUISITION 6 The system is performing a scan that has a scheduled termination such as "at the end of the frame".

docs.title: Enum CcdMode
docs.text:
The CCD mode enumeration.

Name Number Description CCD_MODE_UNSPECIFIED 0 Default enum value. CCD_MODE_OFF 1 Illumination is off. CCD_MODE_AUTO 2 Illumination mode is determined based on detector selection. docs.title: Message ExtendedAcquisitionSettings
docs.text:
Request object to set the simple acquisition settings.

Field Number Type Presence Description detector_name 1 string singular The detector to use. Null will take the detector from the previous acquisition. width 2 int32 singular The image width in pixels. height 3 int32 singular The image height in pixels. dwell_time 4 double singular The dwell time in seconds. The closest dwell time to the selected one will be chosen. frame_averages 5 int32 singular The number of frames to average. 1 means no averaging. line_averages 6 int32 singular The number of lines to average. 1 means no averaging. scan_size_x 7 double singular The relative size of the scan field in x direction proportional to the full field of view, where the FOV equals 1. Range (0, 1]. scan_size_y 8 double singular The relative size of the scan field in y direction proportional to the full field of view, where the FOV equals 1. Range (0, 1]. scan_center_x 9 double singular The relative position of the scan field in x direction proportional to the full field of view, where the optical axis is at (0,0) and the FOV ranges from -0.5 to 0.5. Range (-0.5, 0.5). scan_center_y 10 double singular The relative position of the scan field in y direction proportional to the full field of view, where the optical axis is at (0,0) and the FOV ranges from -0.5 to 0.5. Range (-0.5, 0.5).

docs.title: Enum StageBacklashMode
docs.text:
Stage backlash mode enumeration.

Name Number Description STAGE_BACKLASH_MODE_UNSPECIFIED 0 Unknown indicates that this variable hasn't been assigned yet. STAGE_BACKLASH_MODE_DISABLED 1 Stage backlash is disabled. STAGE_BACKLASH_MODE_POSITIVE 2 Stage backlash is enabled in the positive direction. STAGE_BACKLASH_MODE_NEGATIVE 3 Stage backlash is enabled in the negative direction. STAGE_BACKLASH_MODE_BOTH_DIRECTIONS_POSITIVE 4 Stage backlash is positive in both positive and negative directions. STAGE_BACKLASH_MODE_BOTH_DIRECTIONS_NEGATIVE 5 Stage backlash is negative in both directions.

docs.title: Enum EdsAcquisitionMode
docs.text:
Enum indicating the acquisition mode.

Name Number Description EDS_ACQUISITION_MODE_UNSPECIFIED 0 Default enum value. EDS_ACQUISITION_MODE_AUTO 1 Auto selection of acquisition mode which is Counts. Acquisition continues until enough counts are collected in the spectrum. EDS_ACQUISITION_MODE_LIVE_TIME 2 Acquire EDS data for a period of live time. This is the time for which the system is processing counts into the spectrum. EDS_ACQUISITION_MODE_COUNTS 3 Acquisition continues until enough counts are collected in the spectrum.

docs.title: Enum StageState
docs.text:
Stage state for ZenApi.

Name Number Description STAGE_STATE_UNSPECIFIED 0 Default enum value. STAGE_STATE_UNKNOWN 1 Should not occur in a well configured system. STAGE_STATE_ERROR 2 The stage cannot perform any task. Software restart and/or physical intervention is required. STAGE_STATE_NORMAL 3 The state is functioning normally and can be used. STAGE_STATE_INITIALIZING 4 The stage is in the process of reinitializing one or more axes, should not be used, and will ignore value sets and commands other than stop. STAGE_STATE_INITIALIZATION_NEEDED 5 The stage will respond to motion commands, but positions may be reported erroneously, and the stage should be initialized before further use.

docs.title: Message RegionContour
docs.text:
General data contract for all region contour types.

Field Number Type Presence Description region_ellipse 1 zen_api.lm.acquisition.v1.RegionEllipse oneof subtype region_rectangle 2 zen_api.lm.acquisition.v1.RegionRectangle oneof subtype region_polygon 3 zen_api.lm.acquisition.v1.RegionPolygon oneof subtype

docs.title: Message RegionEllipse
docs.text:
Represents an elliptical region defined by a bounding rectangle.

Field Number Type Presence Description bounding_box 1 zen_api.lm.acquisition.v1.RegionRect singular The rectangle that defines the bounding box of the ellipse. The ellipse is fully contained within this rectangle. The ZenApi.LM.Acquisition.V1.RegionRect specifies the position and size of the bounding rectangle using four values: X (left), Y (top), Width, and Height. For example, a rectangle with X = 10, Y = 20, Width = 100, and Height = 50 defines an ellipse centered at (60, 45) with a horizontal radius of 50 and a vertical radius of 25.

docs.title: Message RegionPolygon
docs.text:
Represents a polygonal region defined by an ordered list of vertices.

Field Number Type Presence Description points 1 zen_api.lm.acquisition.v1.RegionPoint repeated The ordered list of ZenApi.LM.Acquisition.V1.RegionPoint instances that define the vertices of the polygon. Each point specifies an (X, Y) coordinate in the region's coordinate space. The polygon is formed by connecting each consecutive point in the list, and finally connecting the last point back to the first to close the shape.

docs.title: Message RegionRectangle
docs.text:
Represents a rectangular region within the slide scan area.

Field Number Type Presence Description rectangle 1 zen_api.lm.acquisition.v1.RegionRect singular The ZenApi.LM.Acquisition.V1.RegionRect that defines the position and size of the rectangular region within the slide scan area.

docs.title: Message RegionContour
docs.text:
General data contract for all region contour types.

Field Number Type Presence Description name 1 string singular The region contour name. region_ellipse 10 zen_api.lm.acquisition.v2.RegionEllipse oneof subtype region_rectangle 11 zen_api.lm.acquisition.v2.RegionRectangle oneof subtype region_polygon 12 zen_api.lm.acquisition.v2.RegionPolygon oneof subtype

docs.title: Message RegionEllipse
docs.text:
Represents an elliptical region defined by a bounding rectangle.

Field Number Type Presence Description bounding_box 1 zen_api.lm.acquisition.v2.RegionRect singular The rectangle that defines the bounding box of the ellipse. The ellipse is fully contained within this rectangle. The ZenApi.LM.Acquisition.V2.RegionRect specifies the position and size of the bounding rectangle using four values: X (left), Y (top), Width, and Height. For example, a rectangle with X = 10, Y = 20, Width = 100, and Height = 50 defines an ellipse centered at (60, 45) with a horizontal radius of 50 and a vertical radius of 25.

docs.title: Message RegionPolygon
docs.text:
Represents a polygonal region defined by an ordered list of vertices.

Field Number Type Presence Description points 1 zen_api.lm.acquisition.v2.RegionPoint repeated The ordered list of ZenApi.LM.Acquisition.V2.RegionPoint instances that define the vertices of the polygon. Each point specifies an (X, Y) coordinate in the region's coordinate space. The polygon is formed by connecting each consecutive point in the list, and finally connecting the last point back to the first to close the shape.

docs.title: Message RegionRectangle
docs.text:
Represents a rectangular region within the scan area.

Field Number Type Presence Description rectangle 1 zen_api.lm.acquisition.v2.RegionRect singular The ZenApi.LM.Acquisition.V2.RegionRect that defines the position and size of the rectangular region within the scan area.

docs.title: Enum SlideState
docs.text:
This enumeration names all possible slide processing states.

Name Number Description SLIDE_STATE_UNSPECIFIED 0 Default value if status is not specified. SLIDE_STATE_STOPPED 1 Processing was stopped. SLIDE_STATE_NEW 2 New (not processed). SLIDE_STATE_PREVIEW_IN_PROGRESS 3 Preview currently in work. SLIDE_STATE_INPUT_REQUIRED 4 Preview processing finished, but input required. SLIDE_STATE_PREVIEWED 5 Preview processing finished. SLIDE_STATE_SCAN_IN_PROGRESS 6 Scan currently in work. SLIDE_STATE_FINISHED 7 Processing finished. SLIDE_STATE_ERROR 8 Processing error occurred. SLIDE_STATE_SKIPPED 9 Slide was skipped by user.

docs.title: Enum TraySlotState
docs.text:
Enum defining the states of slide scanner slot LEDs.

Name Number Description TRAY_SLOT_STATE_UNSPECIFIED 0 Default value if status is not specified. TRAY_SLOT_STATE_SLOT_OPEN_SYSTEM_PAUSED 1 Slot swiveled out for assembling. TRAY_SLOT_STATE_SLOT_OPEN_TRAY_LOADED 2 Slot swiveled out for assembling but Tray is on stage. TRAY_SLOT_STATE_SLOT_CLOSED_TRAY_NOT_PROCESSED 3 Slot swiveled in with tray containing unprocessed slides. TRAY_SLOT_STATE_SLOT_CLOSED_TRAY_PROCESSED 4 Slot swiveled in with tray containing processed slides. TRAY_SLOT_STATE_SLOT_CLOSED_PROCESS_ERROR 5 Slot swiveled in with tray but an processing error was occurred. TRAY_SLOT_STATE_SLOT_CLOSED_TRAY_PRESCANNED 6 Slot swiveled in with tray containing pre-scanned slides. TRAY_SLOT_STATE_SLOT_CLOSED_TRAY_LOADED 7 Slot swiveled in and tray is on stage. TRAY_SLOT_STATE_SLOT_CLOSED_NO_TRAY 8 Slot swiveled in without tray. TRAY_SLOT_STATE_SLOT_CLOSED_TRAY_IN_SYSTEM_AND_SLOT 9 Slot swiveled in with tray and a tray on the stage (Error case). TRAY_SLOT_STATE_SLOT_CLOSED_UNKNOWN_TRAY 10 Slot swiveled in with an unknown tray type. TRAY_SLOT_STATE_SLOT_CLOSED_NO_SLIDES 11 Slot swiveled in with an empty tray. TRAY_SLOT_STATE_SLOT_CLOSED_TRAY_PARTLY_PROCESSED_WITH_ERRORS 12 Slot swiveled in with tray containing processed slides. TRAY_SLOT_STATE_UNKNOWN 255 Unknown type (tray is inserted but could not be determined).

docs.title: Enum TrayType
docs.text:
Enum defining the types of slide scanner trays.

Name Number Description TRAY_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED 0 Default value if status is not specified. TRAY_TYPE_NONE 1 No tray. TRAY_TYPE_SCAN1X3 2 Scan tray for 4 slides of size 1'x3'. TRAY_TYPE_SCAN2X3 3 Scan tray for 2 slides of size 2'x3'. TRAY_TYPE_SCAN1X3_2X3 4 Scan tray for 2 slides, one of size 1'x3', one of size 2'x3'. TRAY_TYPE_CALIBRATION_STAGE 5 Stage calibration slide holder tray. TRAY_TYPE_SCAN1X3_BASIC 6 Scan tray for 4 slides of size 1'x3', basic design. TRAY_TYPE_SCAN4X3 7 Scan tray for 1 slide of size 4'x3' or a combination of slides of unknown size. TRAY_TYPE_PARKING 152 Arbitrary tray type to indicate the parking position. Is only available at parking position of the magazine changer. TRAY_TYPE_UNKNOWN 153 Unknown type (tray is inserted but could not be determined).

docs.title: Enum JobStatus
docs.text:
Runtime status of the Job.

Name Number Description JOB_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED 0 Default value if status is not specified. JOB_STATUS_RUNNING 1 Job is currently executed by the workflow runner. JOB_STATUS_PAUSED 2 Job execution is paused (not supported for now and reserved only for future purposes for saving numeration sequence). JOB_STATUS_COMPLETED 3 Job execution is successfully completed. JOB_STATUS_FAILED 4 Job execution was failed. JOB_STATUS_CANCELLED 5 Job execution was interrupted (cancelled). JOB_STATUS_PENDING 6 Job is created but still not started and waiting for beginning of execution.

Status of an experiment. The index properties are 0-based. If a value is 0 or -1 it means the value is not initialized or the running experiment does not have the corresponding dimension. In case of indices, 0 value can also refer to the first element.

Attributes:

  • tiles_index (int) –

    The current or already acquired (depending of the dimension order) tiles position index

    The tiles count of the currently acquired scene.

    The total tiles count of all scenes.

    The current or already acquired (depending of the dimension order) scene index (= tile region/position index).

    The total scene count (= tile region/position count).

    The current or already acquired (depending of the dimension order) time point index in time series.

  • time_points_count (int) –

    The number of time points in time series.

    The current or already acquired (depending of the dimension order) z-stack slice index.

  • zstack_slices_count (int) –

    The total count of z-stack slices.

  • channels_index (int) –

    The current or already acquired (depending of the dimension order) channel index.

  • channels_count (int) –

    The total channel count.

  • images_acquired_index (int) –

    The number of acquired images over all dimensions (channels, time series, z-stack, cumulated tiles).

  • images_count (int) –

    The images count over all dimensions (channels, time series, z-stack, cumulated tiles).

  • is_experiment_running (bool) –

    A value indicating whether the experiment is currently running.

  • is_acquisition_running (bool) –

    A value indicating whether an acquisition is currently running.

  • total_elapsed_time (timedelta) –

    The total time that elapsed since the start of the running experiment.

docs.title: create_module async
docs.text:
create_module(
    composition_service_create_module_request: CompositionServiceCreateModuleRequest,
    *,
    timeout: Optional[float] = None,
    deadline: Optional[Deadline] = None,
    metadata: Optional[MetadataLike] = None
) -> CompositionServiceCreateModuleResponse

Creates a module and adds it to the selected profile. With this method, a client can 'inject' a new module at runtime (e.g. via OAD script or ZEN API). After adding the module, it will appear as optional module of the selected profile just as any other module. The Module Manager can be used to verify this. After adding the module, the client can make use of the 'normal' license infrastructure to check the avaiability of the newly added module. Note: A module is available, if the module is licensed AND the user has enabled it (via the Module Manager). In case a module gets added via this method, the module is enabled by default.

Indicates the type of response returned by the camera live image acquisition stream.

Attributes:

docs.title: BeamState
docs.text:
Bases: Enum

Possible beam operating states.

Attributes:

  • UNSPECIFIED –

    Default enum value.

  • UNKNOWN –

    Unknown indicates that this variable hasn't been assigned yet.

  • ERROR –

    There is an error with the Gun or EHT and the beam cannot be used.

  • OFF –

    EHT is off.

  • TURNING_ON –

    The EHT (and gun for C-SEM) is turning on.

  • ON –

    Gun is on.

  • GOING_TO_STANDBY –

    The beam is going into the standby state.

  • STANDBY –

    Not all devices support this mode.

  • TURNING_OFF –

    The EHT is ramping down.

docs.title: UNSPECIFIED class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
UNSPECIFIED = 0

Default enum value.

docs.title: UNKNOWN class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
UNKNOWN = 1

Unknown indicates that this variable hasn't been assigned yet. This value should never occur. If you read this value, it's a bug.

docs.title: ERROR class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
ERROR = 2

There is an error with the Gun or EHT and the beam cannot be used.

docs.title: OFF class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
OFF = 3

EHT is off. On FE-SEMs, the gun may be on, gun interfaces must be checked to discover gun state. On C-SEMs the EHT and gun are off, and there is no current on the filament.

docs.title: TURNING_ON class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
TURNING_ON = 4

The EHT (and gun for C-SEM) is turning on.

docs.title: ON class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
ON = 5

Gun is on. Filament (if it exists) has full current. EHT is on. The beam can be used.

docs.title: GOING_TO_STANDBY class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
GOING_TO_STANDBY = 6

The beam is going into the standby state.

docs.title: STANDBY class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
STANDBY = 7

Not all devices support this mode. This represents an intermediate state. The EVO and the FIB have standby states.

docs.title: TURNING_OFF class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
TURNING_OFF = 8

The EHT is ramping down. On C-SEM, the gun and filament may also be shutting down.

Bases: Enum

Enum indicating the acquisition mode.

Attributes:

  • UNSPECIFIED –

    Default enum value.

  • AUTO –

    Auto selection of acquisition mode which is Counts.

    Acquire EDS data for a period of live time. This is the time for which the system is processing counts into the spectrum.

  • COUNTS –

    Acquisition continues until enough counts are collected in the spectrum.

docs.title: bounding_box class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
bounding_box: RegionRect = betterproto.message_field(1)

The rectangle that defines the bounding box of the ellipse. The ellipse is fully contained within this rectangle. The ZenApi.LM.Acquisition.V1.RegionRect specifies the position and size of the bounding rectangle using four values: X (left), Y (top), Width, and Height. For example, a rectangle with X = 10, Y = 20, Width = 100, and Height = 50 defines an ellipse centered at (60, 45) with a horizontal radius of 50 and a vertical radius of 25.

docs.title: points class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
points: List[RegionPoint] = betterproto.message_field(1)

The ordered list of ZenApi.LM.Acquisition.V1.RegionPoint instances that define the vertices of the polygon. Each point specifies an (X, Y) coordinate in the region's coordinate space. The polygon is formed by connecting each consecutive point in the list, and finally connecting the last point back to the first to close the shape.

docs.title: bounding_box class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
bounding_box: RegionRect = betterproto.message_field(1)

The rectangle that defines the bounding box of the ellipse. The ellipse is fully contained within this rectangle. The ZenApi.LM.Acquisition.V2.RegionRect specifies the position and size of the bounding rectangle using four values: X (left), Y (top), Width, and Height. For example, a rectangle with X = 10, Y = 20, Width = 100, and Height = 50 defines an ellipse centered at (60, 45) with a horizontal radius of 50 and a vertical radius of 25.

The ordered list of ZenApi.LM.Acquisition.V2.RegionPoint instances that define the vertices of the polygon. Each point specifies an (X, Y) coordinate in the region's coordinate space. The polygon is formed by connecting each consecutive point in the list, and finally connecting the last point back to the first to close the shape.

  • FINISHED –

  • ERROR –

    Processing error occurred.

    Slide was skipped by user.

    Slot swiveled in with an empty tray.

docs.title: result_path class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
result_path: str = betterproto.string_field(1)

A value indicating a path for saving a Job results in the file system. -- If value is given than Job output will be copied to given path in filesystem and not uploaded to ZEN Archive. Have to be in the Windows-supported directory path format (local drive or network share). -- If value is null (or empty/whitespace) than Job output will be uploaded to ZEN Archive and not copied to anywhere.

docs.title: JobStatus
docs.text:
Bases: Enum

Runtime status of the Job.

Attributes:

  • UNSPECIFIED –

    Default value if status is not specified.

  • RUNNING –

    Job is currently executed by the workflow runner.

  • PAUSED –

    Job execution is paused (not supported for now and reserved only for future purposes

  • COMPLETED –

    Job execution is successfully completed.

  • FAILED –

    Job execution was failed.

  • CANCELLED –

    Job execution was interrupted (cancelled).

  • PENDING –

    Job is created but still not started and waiting for beginning of execution.

docs.title: UNSPECIFIED class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
UNSPECIFIED = 0

Default value if status is not specified.

docs.title: RUNNING class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
RUNNING = 1

Job is currently executed by the workflow runner.

docs.title: PAUSED class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
PAUSED = 2

Job execution is paused (not supported for now and reserved only for future purposes for saving numeration sequence).

docs.title: COMPLETED class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
COMPLETED = 3

Job execution is successfully completed.

docs.title: FAILED class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
FAILED = 4

Job execution was failed.

docs.title: CANCELLED class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
CANCELLED = 5

Job execution was interrupted (cancelled).

docs.title: PENDING class-attribute instance-attribute

Bases: Enum

Enumerates possible job statuses.

Attributes:

  • UNSPECIFIED –

    Default enum value.

  • NOT_LOADED –

    Job template is not loaded.

  • LOADED –

    Job template is loaded.

  • RUNNING –

    Job is running.

  • FINALIZING –

    Finalizing job results after the job was completed successfully.

  • ARCHIVING –

    Archiving job results after they were finalized.

  • COMPLETED –

    Job was completed successfully.

  • ABORTED –

    Job was aborted.

  • CANCELED –

    Job was canceled.

docs.title: get_cameras_info_LM async
docs.text:
get_cameras_info_LM(
    cameras_service: CameraServiceStub,
) -> list[CameraInfo]

Retrieve comprehensive information about all available cameras.

Queries the ZEN API camera service to get detailed information about all cameras in the system, including their current settings, capabilities, and frame configurations. Converts ZEN API's DoubleFrame and DoubleSize objects to integer-based representations for easier handling.

Parameters:

  • cameras_service (CameraServiceStub) –

    Connected camera service stub for API calls

Returns:

  • list[CameraInfo] –

    list[CameraInfo]: List of camera information objects with converted data types

Raises:

  • Exception –

    If camera service communication fails or camera data is inaccessible

Example

channel, metadata = initialize_zenapi("config.ini") camera_service = CameraServiceStub(channel=channel, metadata=metadata) cameras = await get_cameras_list_LM(camera_service) for camera in cameras: ... print(f"Camera: {camera.name}, Size: {camera.max_frame_size.width}x{camera.max_frame_size.height}")

Retrieve comprehensive information about a specific camera by its ID.

Queries the ZEN API camera service to get detailed information about a specific camera identified by its unique ID, including its current settings, capabilities, and frame configurations. Converts ZEN API's DoubleFrame and DoubleSize objects to integer-based representations for easier handling.

Parameters:

  • cameras_service (CameraServiceStub) –

    Connected camera service stub for API calls

  • camera_id (str) –

    Unique identifier of the camera to retrieve

Returns:

  • CameraInfo ( CameraInfo ) –

    Camera information object with converted data types

Raises:

  • Exception –

    If camera service communication fails or camera ID is invalid

Example

channel, metadata = initialize_zenapi("config.ini") camera_service = CameraServiceStub(channel=channel, metadata=metadata) camera = await get_camera_info_LM(camera_service, "camera_001") print(f"Camera: {camera.name}, Binning: {camera.binning}")

docs.text:
move_changers(
    channel: Channel,
    metadata: list[tuple[str, str]],
    objectives: (
        ObjectiveChangerServiceGetObjectivesResponse | None
    ) = None,
    optovars: (
        OptovarServiceGetOptovarsResponse | None
    ) = None,
    reflectors: (
        ReflectorChangerServiceGetReflectorsResponse | None
    ) = None,
    filters: (
        FilterWheelServiceGetFiltersResponse | None
    ) = None,
    objective_position: int | None = None,
    optovar_position: int | None = None,
    reflector_position: int | None = None,
    filterwheel_position: int | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]

Move microscope changers to specified positions based on keyword arguments. This function is robust and handles situations where not all services are available.

Parameters:

  • channel (Channel) –

    gRPC channel for communication

  • metadata (list[tuple[str, str]]) –

    gRPC metadata for authentication

  • objectives (ObjectiveChangerServiceGetObjectivesResponse | None, default: None ) –

    Available objectives data (optional, will be fetched if service available)

  • optovars (OptovarServiceGetOptovarsResponse | None, default: None ) –

    Available optovars data (optional, will be fetched if service available)

  • reflectors (ReflectorChangerServiceGetReflectorsResponse | None, default: None ) –

    Available reflectors data (optional, will be fetched if service available)

  • filters (FilterWheelServiceGetFiltersResponse | None, default: None ) –

    Available filters data (optional, will be fetched if service available)

  • objective_position (int, default: None ) –

    Target position for objective changer

  • optovar_position (int, default: None ) –

    Target position for optovar changer

  • reflector_position (int, default: None ) –

    Target position for reflector changer

  • filterwheel_position (int, default: None ) –

    Target position for filterwheel changer

Returns:

  • dict ( dict[str, Any] ) –

    Dictionary containing the results of each movement operation with current positions. Includes 'skipped' entries for unavailable services and 'warnings' for service failures.

Note
  • If a service cannot be initialized, the operation will be skipped with a warning
  • Only successfully initialized services will be used for movement operations
  • The function continues execution even if some services fail to initialize
Example

docs.title: This will attempt to move all requested changers, skipping unavailable services
docs.text: results = await move_changers( ... channel=channel, ... metadata=metadata, ... objective_position=2, ... optovar_position=1, ... reflector_position=3, ... filterwheel_position=2 ... ) print(f"Successful moves: {[k for k, v in results.items() if v and v.get('status') == 'success']}") print(f"Skipped services: {results['skipped']}")

    filterwheel_position: int | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]

Advanced version of move_changers that accepts service stubs directly instead of channel & metadata. This is more efficient when you already have service stubs initialized and want to avoid redundant service stub creation. The function is robust and handles situations where not all services are available.

Parameters:

  • objchanger_service (ObjectiveChangerServiceStub, default: None ) –

    Pre-initialized objective changer service

  • optovar_service (OptovarServiceStub, default: None ) –

    Pre-initialized optovar service

  • reflector_service (ReflectorChangerServiceStub, default: None ) –

    Pre-initialized reflector service

  • filterwheel_service (FilterWheelServiceStub, default: None ) –

    Pre-initialized filterwheel service

  • objectives (ObjectiveChangerServiceGetObjectivesResponse | None, default: None ) –

    Available objectives data (optional, will be fetched if None and service available)

  • optovars (OptovarServiceGetOptovarsResponse | None, default: None ) –

    Available optovars data (optional, will be fetched if None and service available)

  • reflectors (ReflectorChangerServiceGetReflectorsResponse | None, default: None ) –

    Available reflectors data (optional, will be fetched if None and service available)

  • filters (FilterWheelServiceGetFiltersResponse | None, default: None ) –

    Available filters data (optional, will be fetched if None and service available)

  • objective_position (int, default: None ) –

    Target position for objective changer

  • optovar_position (int, default: None ) –

    Target position for optovar changer

  • reflector_position (int, default: None ) –

    Target position for reflector changer

  • filterwheel_position (int, default: None ) –

    Target position for filterwheel changer

Returns:

  • dict ( dict[str, Any] ) –

    Dictionary containing the results of each movement operation with current positions. Includes 'skipped' entries for unavailable services and 'warnings' for missing services.

Note
  • If a position is specified but the corresponding service is not available, the operation will be skipped
  • Only available services will be used for movement operations
  • The function continues execution even if some services are unavailable
Example

docs.title: Only objective and optovar services available
docs.text: objchanger_service = ObjectiveChangerServiceStub(channel=channel, metadata=metadata) optovar_service = OptovarServiceStub(channel=channel, metadata=metadata)

docs.title: This will move objective and optovar, skip reflector and filterwheel

docs.title: zen_api_utils.extract_czexp_plan
docs.text:
Extract a provisional CZI/CZMBI acquisition plan from a ZEN Experiment XML file.

Disclaimer: This script is intended for experimental use and may not cover all edge cases of ZEN Experiment XML files.

Run from the repository root:

python experimental\extract_czexp_plan.py experimental\ZEN_API_Test_CD7_split.czexp

Write a reduced JSON plan and a CZMBI file in one call:

python experimental\extract_czexp_plan.py `
    experimental\ZEN_API_Test_CD7_split.czexp `
    --reduced `
    --output experimental\plan.json `
    --czmbi-output experimental\hcs.czmbi

The JSON plan is always written first. When --czmbi-output is present, the script reloads that JSON and projects its first acquisition block to CZMBI 1.0. CZMBI generation requires split-scene acquisition with one planned CZI per scene. When ZEN does not expose exact output names, the generated CZMBI uses deterministic suggested_filename values that must be validated against actual ZEN output.

docs.title: open_in_ndv_viewer
docs.text:
open_in_ndv_viewer(zarr_path: Path) -> None

Open an OME-ZARR dataset in the ndv viewer.

Reads axis names (T, C, Z, Y, X) and per-axis scales from the OME-ZARR 0.5 metadata stored in zarr.json and wraps the highest-resolution array as a dask-backed xr.DataArray with physically-spaced coordinates so that ndv shows correct proportions (including Z depth) and labelled sliders.

Requires optional dependencies: ndv, zarr, dask, xarray. If any are missing the function logs a warning and returns silently.

Parameters:

  • zarr_path (Path) –

    Path to the .ome.zarr directory.

docs.title: read_omezarr_axis_names
docs.text:
read_omezarr_axis_names(
    zarr_path: Path,
) -> tuple[str, ...] | None

Read axis names from the first OME-ZARR 0.5 image metadata.

OME-ZARR 0.5 (zarr v3) stores the multiscales metadata inside zarr.json → attributes.ome.multiscales, unlike OME-ZARR 0.4 which used .zattrs.

Parameters:

  • zarr_path (Path) –

    Path to the .ome.zarr directory.

Returns:

  • tuple[str, ...] | None –

    Tuple of uppercase axis names (e.g. ('T', 'C', 'Z', 'Y', 'X')),

  • tuple[str, ...] | None –

    or None if the metadata cannot be read.

docs.title: read_omezarr_axis_scales
docs.text:
read_omezarr_axis_scales(
    zarr_path: Path,
) -> dict[str, float] | None

Read scale factors from the first OME-ZARR 0.5 image metadata.

The scale transform is stored in zarr.json → attributes.ome.multiscales[0].datasets[0].coordinateTransformations as a list entry with {"type": "scale", "scale": [s0, s1, ...]}. The scale values are ordered to match the axes list.

Parameters:

  • zarr_path (Path) –

    Path to the .ome.zarr directory.

Returns:

  • dict[str, float] | None –

    Dict mapping uppercase axis name to its scale factor,

  • dict[str, float] | None –

    or None if the metadata cannot be read.

docs.title: stream_to_omezarr async
docs.text:
stream_to_omezarr(
    zenapi_config: str | Path,
    experiment_name: str,
    output_dir: str | Path,
    dtype: dtype | None = None,
    start_experiment_from_script: bool = False,
    czi_name: str = "zenapi_stream",
    overwrite_czi: bool = True,
    channel_index: int | None = None,
    overwrite_zarr: bool = True,
    compression: str | None = "blosc-zstd",
    spatial_shard_size_chunks: int | None = 2,
    inactivity_timeout: float = _STATUS_POLL_TIMEOUT,
) -> Path

Stream ZEN pixel data into an OME-ZARR file.

Parameters:

  • zenapi_config (str | Path) –

    Path to the ZEN-API gateway config.ini.

  • experiment_name (str) –

    ZEN experiment name (without .czexp).

  • output_dir (str | Path) –

    Folder where the OME-ZARR will be created.

  • dtype (dtype | None, default: None ) –

    Pixel data type (must match the experiment output).

  • start_experiment_from_script (bool, default: False ) –

    If True, start the experiment via API. If False, the user starts the experiment from the ZEN UI.

  • czi_name (str, default: 'zenapi_stream' ) –

    CZI output name when starting experiment from script.

  • overwrite_czi (bool, default: True ) –

    Allow overwriting an existing CZI.

  • channel_index (int | None, default: None ) –

    Optional channel filter index (None = all channels).

  • overwrite_zarr (bool, default: True ) –

    Overwrite an existing OME-ZARR at the output path.

  • compression (str | None, default: 'blosc-zstd' ) –

    Compression for ZARR ('blosc-zstd', 'blosc-lz4', 'zstd', 'none', or None).

  • spatial_shard_size_chunks (int | None, default: 2 ) –

    Number of chunks per Y/X shard, or None to disable Zarr v3 sharding.

  • inactivity_timeout (float, default: _STATUS_POLL_TIMEOUT ) –

    Maximum wait for another matching frame. Missing expected coordinates fail the acquisition.

Returns:

  • Path –

    Path to the created OME-ZARR directory.

Raises:

  • IncompleteAcquisitionError –

    Expected frames are missing. Partial data and a completion report are retained, without finalization.

docs.title: stream_to_omezarr_with_config async
docs.text:
stream_to_omezarr_with_config(
    ecfg: ExperimentConfig,
    inactivity_timeout: float = _STATUS_POLL_TIMEOUT,
) -> Path

Stream ZEN pixel data into OME-ZARR using exported experiment dimensions.

Export the selected experiment before opening channel subscriptions. The first matching frame supplies its pixel size and live dimensions; subsequent frames are written with bounded out-of-order buffering.

Parameters:

  • ecfg (ExperimentConfig) –

    Writer and experiment settings. Exported metadata replaces dimension hints without mutating this configuration object.

  • inactivity_timeout (float, default: _STATUS_POLL_TIMEOUT ) –

    Maximum wait for another matching frame.

Returns:

  • Path –

    Path to the created OME-ZARR directory.

Raises:

  • IncompleteAcquisitionError –

    Expected frames are missing. Partial data and a completion report are retained, without finalization.
